subject: psychology
title: Schizophrenia & Depression: Diagnosis & Classification
welcome_lead: DSM and ICD compete; reliability and validity wobble.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology schizophrenia depression diagnosis DSM ICD reliability validity.
final_note: Diagnosis is a social act — not a blood test.

concepts.def: International Classification of Diseases — WHO classification.
Lost normal function — avolition, alogia, flat affect.
Same symptom appearing in multiple disorders.

walkthroughs.body_html: DSM-5 (2013) requires one positive symptom (hallucinations, delusions or disorganised speech) for schizophrenia. ICD-11 (2022) requires two symptoms for one month. Subtypes (paranoid, catatonic) were dropped in DSM-5 as unreliable.

Two clinicians must give the same diagnosis to a patient — inter-rater reliability. Cheniaux et al. (2009) had two psychiatrists diagnose 100 patients: only 26 received the same diagnosis under both DSM and ICD systems. Reliability is mixed.

Symptoms overlap with bipolar disorder. Co-morbidity with depression occurs in ~50% of schizophrenia cases (Buckley 2009). Gender bias: women diagnosed less due to better social function (Cotton 2009). Culture bias: Afro-Caribbean men in UK over-diagnosed (Pinto & Jones 2008).
